strengths: Unified booking model: one health.fieldservice.order carries scheduling, staff, clinical notes, quote, invoice and compliance state — competitors typically fragment this across 3-4 systems.
Offline-first nurse PWA with payment collection in the field — most competitors' mobile apps are online-only or read-mostly.
Visual Blockly pricing engine with plain-language rule explanations and approval workflow — genuinely rare; most competitors hard-code rate tables.
Semantic BI layer with governed LLM chart generation (metadata-only, provider-pluggable including local Ollama) — ahead of most home-care vendors' static reporting.
Deep Vietnam compliance moat: Viettel Red Invoice, MISA sync, Vietnamese address/kinship structures, Zalo-native communications, TET pricing.
AI assignment engine with scheduled optimization and a reusable multi-provider AI framework already in production.
Theme token engine + workspace shells give a design-system foundation most Odoo (and healthcare) products lack.
Catchment-province access model cleanly supports geographic multi-branch operations.
Relationship-first CRM (client ↔ caregiver/payer/referrer/guardian) matches the reality that home-care buyers are usually family members, not patients.
weaknesses: Clinical depth is thin: clinical documentation is largely free text; no care plans, structured vitals, eMAR, incidents, or wound tracking — this is the biggest gap vs. AlayaCare/WellSky-class platforms.
Client-facing surface is nearly zero: portal is a stub, no self-booking, no family visibility, no telehealth — competitors monetize family engagement heavily.
Zero interoperability: no FHIR/HL7/SNOMED/ICD/LOINC and no enterprise API gateway, blocking government programs, insurers, and ASEAN national platforms (e.g. SATUSEHAT).
Scheduling lacks route optimization, shift swaps, and true recurring-series generation — the roster is visual but not yet intelligent about geography.
Visit verification is not EVV-grade: GPS points exist but no geofencing, no signatures, no tamper-evident audit — a blocker for government-funded programs in AU/US-style markets.
Notifications are one-way and manual: no SMS/Zalo reminder automation, no secure two-way client messaging.
Compliance posture is Vietnam-only: no consent management, no GDPR/HIPAA-grade audit and data-residency story for expansion markets.
Vitals stored as free text prevents trending, alerting, and any predictive clinical AI until structured.

items: Care plan model with goals, interventions, review cycles
Structured vitals with LOINC coding, trending, alert thresholds
Assessment library beyond Morse falls (pain, nutrition, cognition, ADL, pressure injury)
Wound care tracking with photo timeline
Structured progress notes with outcome trending
SNOMED CT / ICD-10 / LOINC terminology service
Country adapters (VN MOH, Singapore NEHR, Indonesia SATUSEHAT, AU My Health Record/NDIS)
Enterprise API gateway (OpenAPI, keys, rate limits, webhooks)
Recurring series auto-generation and bulk reschedule
